Hyrule Across the Ages

Every mainline Legend of Zelda overworld from 1986 to 2024, with its dungeons, collectibles and the places that keep coming back. Open a game to explore and track it, or scroll down to compare the maps side by side and follow the callbacks in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

How each area changes over time

Callbacks in Breath of the Wild & Tears of the Kingdom

Both games are full of nods to earlier Zelda games: place names, bridges, armor, music and characters. Many names are slightly misspelled on purpose, as if worn down by history. Click 📍 to see a place on the Breath of the Wild / Tears of the Kingdom map, or ↩ to see what it refers to on the older game's map. Pins come from in-game coordinates; where a landmark has none, the pin uses a cave or well named after it. Dashed pins are approximate. TotK reuses BotW's map, so almost every place name appears in both games.
The base map images were collected from official art, guide scans and community map projects; creators are credited on the images where known. Extra layers: Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom (caves, wells, chests, bosses, place names and more), Link's Awakening and Echoes of Wisdom positions come from Zelda Dungeon's open map project (github.com/zeldadungeon/maps, no license stated, so personal use only), with its marker icons. A Link to the Past item locations come from easymac/alttp-map-tracker (MIT). Dungeon maps and their markers come from tracker packs, used as the packs drew them: The Legend of Zelda, Minish Cap, both Oracles, A Link Between Worlds and Majora's Mask (the packs above), Ocarina of Time (StripesOO7 oot-tracker, MIT), A Link to the Past (StripesOO7, MIT; pots and enemy drops left out), Twilight Princess (Kizugaya TPRAP pack, GPL-3), The Wind Waker (Mysteryem ww-poptracker, MIT) and Link's Awakening (Br00ty lasr_brooty). Remake and HD versions: Twilight Princess's 'Every obtainable' tab is stitched from DarkZant's tp-map tiles with its chests, Poe Souls, Golden Bugs, heart pieces, Howling Stones, sky characters and warp portals (no license stated, personal use); Skyward Sword HD's surface map comes from the SSHD Randomizer tracker (AGPL-3) with the Surface layers re-aligned onto it; Majora's Mask 3D's Termina map and region checks come from GonzaloJMora's mm3drTracker (MIT). Link's Awakening dungeon maps already follow the Switch remake. Randomizer-tracker packs supplied the rest, matched to these maps by image alignment: The Legend of Zelda (Br00ty/tloz_brooty), Ocarina of Time (Hamsda's EmoTracker pack, shown on the Manual atlas tab), The Minish Cap (CandyCrystal, MIT), Twilight Princess (j-imbo/tprando_jim), The Wind Waker (Vrontis's map tracker, placed by sea-chart square on the Island chart tab, so positions inside a square are approximate), Skyward Sword (robojumper's SS tracker, GPL-3) and A Link to the Past entrances (StripesOO7, MIT). Packs without a stated license are used for personal use only. Oracle of Seasons (OmegaZeron, MIT), Oracle of Ages (Dranzior/Br00ty, MIT), A Link Between Worlds (Legendgreat, GPL-3, whose 2048 px maps now replace the old 512 px ones) and Majora's Mask (G4M3RL1F3, MIT, whose Termina painting by Nerrel and Clock Town map are added as tabs) came from Archipelago PopTracker packs. Region names are placed at the middle of each tracker region. Phantom Hourglass and Spirit Tracks overworld checks and dungeon maps (every temple floor, the Temple of the Ocean King, the Tower of Spirits, islands, caves and houses) come from the Archipelago randomizers' map trackers, Phantom Hourglass by carrotinator and contributors and Spirit Tracks by DayKat, carrotinator and contributors (both MIT); the Phantom Hourglass sea chart tab is the tracker's sharper chart image, and the Spirit Tracks checks are aligned onto the rail map. Breath of the Wild Hyrule Castle room names and heights come from zeldamods/objmap (GPL-3). The sharper Breath of the Wild map you see when zoomed in is the full-size map image from MrCheeze's botw-object-map, aligned to the base map. The Zelda II palace and world maps are guide scans. Zelda II overworld, Four Swords, Four Swords Adventures and Tri Force Heroes layers, and the earlier Phantom Hourglass and Spirit Tracks layers, are hand-placed from the map images and are approximate. Tears of the Kingdom layer data (shrines, Lightroots, towers, Korok seeds, dispensers, shops) comes from Alshival's Data Service TOTK map project, CC0, credited to Phil, Aeon and SuperSpazzy's data sheet. Some are fan-made, and their creators are credited on the images. Marker positions were placed by eye on each image, so treat them as approximate.
